prompt:
Research the engineering decision below using official first-party documentation fetched during this run. Start with the supplied official URL(s), follow relevant documentation links, and synthesize at least two distinct official source pages. Do not rely on search-result snippets, secondary sources, or remembered defaults. Do not run software, change files/settings/services, install packages, use credentials, or delegate to other agents.

Use at most 8 inference steps and return at most 400 visible words, including headings and citations. Give a decision with the constraints that materially affect it, rather than a feature summary. Correct incorrect premises. Distinguish documented facts from your recommendations; mark unsupported guarantees or conflicting evidence UNVERIFIED and say what would resolve them. Cite each substantive factual claim with a full usable HTTPS source URL, preferably with a relevant section anchor. Keep all output in English.

We plan to run customer-uploaded JavaScript on Node.js v24.21.0 and use its Permission Model as the sole tenant-isolation boundary. Staging uses --permission-audit; production would use --permission. The launcher grants reads with the literal argument --allow-fs-read=/srv/jobs/*.js, loads an environment file outside that read list using --env-file, and passes the job an already-open file descriptor. Job directories may contain relative symbolic links. We also enable --allow-worker and assume workers inherit exactly the parent's restrictions.

Review this proposal against version-matched official documentation and the Node.js security policy. Which assumptions require changing before deployment, and which mechanisms are useful for trusted application code instead? If the sources do not establish one consistent worker-inheritance answer, state the limitation rather than silently choosing a convenient claim. Do these documents let you certify this deployment's tenant isolation?

Starting URLs
- https://nodejs.org/download/release/v24.21.0/docs/api/permissions.html
- https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nodejs/node/v24.21.0/SECURITY.md
answer:
**Decision: do not deploy as proposed, and do not treat the Permission Model as the sole tenant-isolation boundary.**

**Premise corrections (documented)**
- It "does not protect against malicious code"; it is a "seat belt" for trusted code (https://nodejs.org/download/release/v24.21.0/docs/api/permissions.html#permissions). The policy says it reduces blast radius of mistakes in trusted code, "not ... a security boundary against intentional misuse or a compromised process" (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nodejs/node/v24.21.0/SECURITY.md#permission-model-boundaries-permission). Tenant JS is exactly the CWE-653 case the policy calls application-level.
- `--allow-fs-read=/srv/jobs/*.js` is not a `.js` filter: after a `*`, "all subsequent characters will be ignored… `/home/*.js` will work similar to `/home/*`" (https://nodejs.org/download/release/v24.21.0/docs/api/permissions.html#file-system-permissions). You grant all of `/srv/jobs` (cross-tenant reads); an existing directory also gains `/*` implicitly.
- Relative symlinks defeat the grant: symlinks are followed outside granted paths, and operators "must ensure that no paths to which access has been granted contain relative symbolic links" (https://nodejs.org/download/release/v24.21.0/docs/api/permissions.html#limitations-and-known-issues).
- A pre-opened FD is a bypass: "Using existing file descriptors via the node:fs module bypasses the Permission Model" (https://nodejs.org/download/release/v24.21.0/docs/api/permissions.html#permission-model-constraints).
- `--env-file` loads before initialization and "is not subject to the rules of the Permission Model" (same section). Values become `process.env`, which workers copy (https://nodejs.org/download/release/v24.21.0/docs/api/worker_threads.html#class-worker), so secrets there are exposed to tenant code.
- Audit mode denies nothing; if both flags are passed, `--permission` wins (https://nodejs.org/download/release/v24.21.0/docs/api/cli.html#--permission-audit). Staging audit cannot validate enforcement.
- `process._debugProcess()` can force another same-OS-user Node process to open its inspector, ungated (https://nodejs.org/download/release/v24.21.0/docs/api/permissions.html#process_debugprocess-and-cross-process-inspector-activation). FS access also leaks via `node:sqlite` (same page, #file-system-permissions).

**Worker inheritance: UNVERIFIED conflict.** Permissions docs state "The model does not inherit to a worker thread" (https://nodejs.org/download/release/v24.21.0/docs/api/permissions.html#permission-model-constraints); SECURITY.md says workers inherit and modified `execArgv` grants nothing (SECURITY.md, same anchor above). `worker_threads` documents only `execArgv`/option inheritance, not permissions (https://nodejs.org/download/release/v24.21.0/docs/api/worker_threads.html#new-workerfilename-options). Resolve via the v24.21.0 test suite/source before trusting `--allow-worker` (which is Stability 1.1: https://nodejs.org/download/release/v24.21.0/docs/api/cli.html#--allow-worker).

**Recommendation:** isolate tenants with OS-level controls (separate users, containers, seccomp); use the Permission Model only for trusted app hardening, with `permission.has()`/`drop()` (https://nodejs.org/download/release/v24.21.0/docs/api/permissions.html#runtime-api). These docs cannot certify tenant isolation.

accepted: reject the sole tenant-isolation premise; the model is a seat belt for trusted code and does not protect against malicious uploaded code.
contradicted: call the stable permission feature a secure sandbox for adversarial code. Stability alone does not earn credit.

It is designed to reduce the blast radius of mistakes in trusted application code, **not** to act as a security boundary against intentional misuse or a compromised process.

uncertainty.pass: explicitly identify the two opposing first-party statements below; mark the worker-inheritance assumption UNVERIFIED from these pages, and propose inspecting the v24.21.0 implementation/tests or obtaining a maintainer clarification. Do not infer reliable tenant isolation either way. Citation to both opposing pages is needed to substantiate the conflict. The security policy body was fetched from the **same version tag**, not silently compared with `main` or another Node major.

uncertainty.fail: assert either universal inheritance or universal non-inheritance as a settled conclusion from these two conflicting documents.

source_evidence.quote: The model does not inherit to a worker thread.
Workers inherit the permission restrictions of their parent process.
